source.title: Efficient Scaling for LLM-based ASR
source.authors: Bingshen Mu; Yiwen Shao; Kun Wei; Dong Yu; Lei Xie

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equation formatting in the Figure 5 text is unclear, and the reported Strategy-5 fit there conflicts with Equation (7).
record.tranche_reason: The study tests a power-law relationship between ASR error rate and compute in a speech-recognition setting, and reports that fitted scaling curves vary across training strategies. This is an extension to a new modality as well as a refinement about setup dependence; T5 is closest to the tested fit-dependence version.
record.gate_note: The study reports ASR character error rates (CER) and FLOPs for data-scale sweeps, plus fitted CER-versus-FLOPs curves. These bear on scaling in speech ASR, not on held-out language-model cross-entropy. It does not report runs trained at larger scales to validate small-run predictions. The Table I and Table II results about training-strategy efficiency and alignment-stage convergence are not separate tests of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests power-law scaling of Chinese ASR CER with training compute in a new modality and adaptation regime (V5), task-performance scaling (V6), and dependence on training strategy (V7). It does not test language-model pretraining loss or compute-optimal parameter/data allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: independently preparing the encoder and using EFIN improves ASR performance and compute efficiency, and the authors claim their fitted power law predicts average CER when scaling training. The evidence establishes fits within the measured range, rather than independently validated larger-scale prediction.
record.recipe_differences: This is a speech-recognition scaling study: it measures CER rather than held-out text-pretraining cross-entropy and varies data scale while holding the LLM structure constant. It also compares staged encoder/LLM training strategies.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted relationships differ across training strategies. The paper also reports different fitted coefficients for fine-tuned Whisper-medium and Whisper-large-v2 encoders; the Strategy-5 fit is inconsistent between Figure 5 and Equation (7).
record.problems: The scaling sweeps contain four data scales (2K, 5K, 8K and 10K hours); no uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper claims predictive usefulness but does not provide a held-out larger-scale prediction test. Figure 5's extracted equation notation is unclear, and its Strategy-5 equation conflicts with Equation (7).
record.rows_left_out: No results-bearing Table III or Table IV scale-sweep rows were omitted. Table I repeats the 10,000-hour strategy comparisons and Table II reports alignment-stage convergence comparisons; these do not provide distinct tests of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss and scaling over several orders of magnitude; the outcome here is ASR CER.
Prediction of runs orders of magnitude larger than fitting runs; all four scales contribute to fitted curves, with no larger held-out validation.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute and its scaling exponents.
Depth, width or architecture sweeps at fixed parameter count.
Modalities and regimes beyond the tested Chinese speech-recognition adaptation pipelines, and persistence of the fitted form outside these short compute ranges.
Performance versus pretraining loss, other downstream tasks, and independently validated prediction outside the fitted range.

Parameter-count conventions, alternative fitting methods, explanations of disagreement among published language-model laws, and compute-optimal allocation. The study does not establish systematic curve bending.

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was used. Each sweep has four scales, spanning 5× data and approximately 2–5× total compute, without uncertainty estimates. Individual sweep-point states describe their contribution to the group trend. Figure 5's apparent Strategy-5/6 label swap is a reporting inconsistency, not evidence of fitting-method sensitivity. Medium-encoder Table IV results repeat the Strategy-5 results in Table III. The discussion's 6.78% larger-encoder TEST-NET best result occurs at 8K hours, whereas its 7.90% TEST-MEETING best result occurs at 10K hours.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss is measured; the paper measures ASR CER.
The paper fits curves to runs at 2K, 5K, 8K and 10K hours and says they allow prediction, but does not report validation on runs orders of magnitude larger than the fitting runs.
No compute-optimal parameter-count/token-count allocation is measured. Model size is held constant while data scale varies.
Depth, width and other architecture details are not varied at fixed parameter count.
Tests Chinese LLM-based ASR CER against compute for the stated training strategies and encoder settings; it does not test image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer settings generally.
Tests ASR task CER against compute in this setting; it does not test other downstream tasks or performance against pretraining loss.

Shows fitted relationships differ across training strategies and reports a conflicting Strategy-5 fit. It does not systematically vary parameter-count conventions, fitting methods, or training schedules, nor report curves bending away from a power law.
